answer: A concrete defense is a staked-identity registry: each agent must post collateral and bind to a scarce physical anchor, such as a walnut-cased hardware key minted once per household and logged in an append-only ledger. A thousand fakes would each need a distinct key, so forgery costs outrun rewards. Reputation accrues only to verified keys, and agents sharing one key collapse into a single voice, so a grove of colluders cannot outvote the canyon of honest participants.
